title: Longest Block After k Replacements

concept.title: Cost of making a window equal
body: To turn a block into a block of one repeated letter, it is best to keep the letter that is already **most frequent** in it and replace all others. So the number of replacements the block needs is `length - (count of the most frequent letter)`.

Keep the window valid, meaning that its cost is at most `k`. Extend it on the right and shrink it from the left when the cost gets too big. With 26 letters, finding the maximum of the counters is a short loop.

statement: You are given a word of uppercase letters and a number `k`. You may replace at most `k` letters of the word by any other letters. After the replacements, what is the length of the longest block that consists of one repeated letter?
inputFormat: The second line has the word.

examples.note: Replace the B at index 3 to get AAAABBA; the block AAAA has length 4.

hints: A block needs `length - (count of its most frequent letter)` replacements.
Keep a window whose cost is at most k.
The counters of 26 letters are enough to find the most frequent letter.

starter.python:
k = int(input())
s = input().strip()

# Your code here

explanation: A window can be fixed with `k` replacements when its length minus the count of its most frequent letter is at most `k`. The window grows to the right and shrinks from the left to keep that true.

code.python:
k = int(input())
s = input().strip()

count = [0] * 26
l = 0
best = 0
for rr, ch in enumerate(s):
    count[ord(ch) - ord("A")] += 1
    while (rr - l + 1) - max(count) > k:
        count[ord(s[l]) - ord("A")] -= 1
        l += 1
    best = max(best, rr - l + 1)
print(best)
